text:
Recent work supports behavioral interventions alongside embedding diagnostics. [Robust Training (2024)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) finds strong sensitivity to removing recent interactions and measures ranking changes using Rank List Sensitivity and rank-biased overlap; its experiments concern GRU/SASRec variants, so BERT4Rec transfer requires measurement. [Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042) shows that apparent sequential signal can originate from user behavior, item availability, or both; availability-constrained shuffling helps distinguish them. [Counterfactual explanations (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) investigate minimal history edits that change recommendations. Such changes establish model sensitivity, not necessarily causal effects on user preferences.

[Sampling Reliability (RecSys 2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines sampled evaluation’s resolution, agreement with full-ranking results, and robustness to exposure bias, reporting 95% intervals from 1,000 bootstrap resamples. [Improved Rank Estimation (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) likewise addresses negative-sampling bias. Practical synthesis: on training-only prefixes with withheld targets, compare recent versus equally sized older-history removal, order shuffling, and popularity-matched replacements. For BERT4Rec, exclude the target from history and score an appended mask. Pair original/perturbed examples on identical candidates; report target-rank, HR@10, margin, and ranking-overlap changes, stratified by training popularity and history length. Bootstrap users, keeping each user’s prefixes together; separately repeat diagnostic candidate draws to expose sampling variability. These are proposed controls, not one established protocol. Keep host validation unchanged; full-catalog diagnostics and representation effective rank are supplementary evidence, not substitute selection metrics.
